verses.zh: 祸哉！你这毁灭人的，自己倒不被毁灭；行事诡诈的，人倒不以诡诈待你。你毁灭罢休了，自己必被毁灭；你行完了诡诈，人必以诡诈待你。
verses.en: The destroyer is as good as dead,[NOTE:1] you who have not been destroyed!The deceitful one is as good as dead,[NOTE:2] the one whom others have not deceived!When you are through destroying, you will be destroyed;when you finish[NOTE:3] deceiving, others will deceive you!
notes: Heb “Woe [to] the destroyer.”sn In this context “the destroyer” appears to refer collectively to the hostile nations (vv. 3-4). Assyria would probably have been primary in the minds of the prophet and his audience.
Heb “and the deceitful one”; NAB, NIV84 “O traitor”; NIV11 “you betrayer”; NRSV “you treacherous one.” In the parallel structure הוֹי (hoy, “woe [to]”) does double duty.

The form in the Hebrew text appears to derive from an otherwise unattested verb נָלָה (nalah). The translation follows the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa in reading ככלתך, a Piel infinitival form from the verbal root כָּלָה (kalah), meaning “finish.”
verses.commentary:
33:1 "Woe" Isaiah 28-33 forms a unit often called the "Unit of Doom" because of the recurrent use of the
term "woe," (cf. Isa. 28:1; 29:1,15; 30:1; 31:1; 33:1). See note on "Woe" at Isa. 5:8.

▣ "O destroyer" Isaiah 33:1 speaks of Assyria, as does Isa. 33:3,4,7-9,11-12,17-19,23; even
Isa. 33:21 may refer to the cities located on the Tigris and Euphrates. This chapter follows a common
theme pattern of Isaiah.

- the current rebellious state of God's people

- God's judgment by foreign powers

- God's judgment of these foreign powers (here Assyria)

- the future glorious conditions of His people through the righteous king (cf. Isa. 32:1)

The Hebrew root שׁדד (BDB 994, KB 1418)
is used four times in this verse.

- "O destroyer" ‒ Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- "not destroyed" ‒ Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE

- "destroying" ‒ Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- "will be destroyed" ‒ Qal PASSIVE IMPERFECT

Also, the Hebrew root בגד (BDB 93, KB 108)
is also used four times.

- "he who is treacherous" ‒ Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- "others did not deal treacherously with him" ‒ Qal PERFECT

- "as soon as you shall cease to deal treacherously" ‒ Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- "others shall deal treacherously with you" ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

It is common in Isaiah to repeat NOUNS, VERBS for effect. This
repetition was normal and expected! These roots are also used in Isa. 21:2 about the fall of old Babylon. In a theological
sense Isaiah's ambiguity is purposeful. He intentionally makes the identity of Israel/Judah's aggressors fuzzy so that
his poems can function as "multiple-fulfillment" prophecies. Enemies come and go by YHWH's hand and purpose, but
YHWH Himself and His eternal redemptive purpose, using Abraham's seed, does not!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"cease"

NJB, JPSOA, NET
"finished"

In line 5 the MT has the VERBAL (BDB 649, KB 701, Hiphil
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT), which is found only here. Most translations, ancient and
modern, follow the DSS, which has "to complete" or "to finish" (BDB 477, KB 476, Piel
INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT), used often in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 1:28; 10:18,25; 15:6; 16:4; 21:16;
24:13; 27:10; 29:20; 31:3; 32:10; 49;4).

- BDB 649, כנלתך

- BDB 477, ככלתך

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你施恩于我们；我们等候你。求你每早晨作我们的膀臂，遭难的时候为我们的拯救。
verses.en: Lord, be merciful to us! We wait for you.Give us strength each morning.[NOTE:1] Deliver us when distress comes.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Be their arm each morning.” “Arm” is a symbol for strength. The mem suffixed to the noun has been traditionally understood as a third person suffix, but this is contrary to the context, where the people speak of themselves in the first person. The mem (מ) is probably enclitic with ellipsis of the pronoun, which can be supplied from the context. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:589, n. 1.
Heb “[Be] also our deliverance in the time of distress.”
verses.commentary:
33:2 The content of Judah's prayer is delineated.

- be gracious to us, BDB 335, KB 334, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Isa. 30:18,19

- we have waited for You, BDB 875 I, KB 1082, Piel PERFECT,
cf. Isa. 8:17; 25:9; 26:8; 40:31; 49:23; 51:5; 60:9

- be our strength (lit. "arm") every morning, BDB 224, KB 243, Qal
IMPERATIVE

- be our salvation in time of distress ("be" VERB assumed)

YHWH is Judah's only hope (cf. Isa. 59:16; 63:1,5), not Assyria (alliance) and not Egypt
(alliance), only YHWH. Humans tend to panic and lose trust in times of crisis and uncertainty. They
try to save themselves using their resources or the resources of other humans, to no avail!

▣ "strength" It is literally "arm" (BDB 283). This is a biblical anthropomorphic imagery to
describe YHWH's presence and power on a daily basis.

▣ "salvation" This term (BDB 447) is commonly used in the OT for physical deliverance (cf.
Isa. 12:2 [twice], 3; 25:9; 26:1,18; 33:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT term)

verses.zh: 喧嚷的响声一发，众民奔逃；你一兴起，列国四散。
verses.en: The nations run away when they hear a loud noise;[NOTE:1] the nations scatter when you spring into action![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “at the sound of tumult the nations run away.”
Heb “because of your exaltation the nations scatter.”
verses.commentary:
33:3

NASB, Peshitta
"the lifting up of Yourself"

NKJV
"when You lift Yourself up"

NRSV
"before your majesty"

TEV
"when you fight for us"

NJB
"when you stand up"

JPSOA
"before Your majesty"

The NOUN (BDB 928, KB 1206) occurs only here and its meaning is uncertain,
but it seems to be related to "extolling praise" (BDB 928). The UBS Text Project, p. 74, gives "at the lifting up (the voice)"
a "C" rating (considerable doubt). It seems there is a parallel with line one, therefore, some type of shout or noise. However, the
NRSV, JPSOA, and NET think it refers to YHWH's actions, which fits the meaning of the verse better..

verses.zh: 你们所掳的必被敛尽，好像蚂蚱吃（原文是敛）尽禾稼。人要蹦在其上，好像蝗虫一样。
verses.en: Your plunder[NOTE:1] disappears as if locusts were eating it;[NOTE:2] they swarm over it like locusts.[NOTE:3]
notes: The pronoun is plural; the statement is addressed to the nations who have stockpiled plunder from their conquests of others.
Heb “and your plunder is gathered, the gathering of the locust.”
Heb “like a swarm of locusts swarming on it.”
verses.commentary:
33:4 In this verse "spoil"(BDB 1021) is imagery which denotes the destruction of YHWH's enemies.

The VERB "gathered" (BDB 62, KB 74, Pual
PERFECT with waw) is also used in

- Isa. 32:10 to describe the judgment of Jerusalem

- Isa. 24:22 (same stem) to denote worldwide eschatological judgment

Humans "gather" for self, greed, and power, but God gathers for judgment. The NT describes
the end-time gathering of

- the redeemed, Matt. 13:36-43,47-50; 24:31

- the wicked, Matt. 13:40-41

▣ "locusts" Locust invasions were common in the ANE. They are often compared to an invading
army (cf. Deut. 28:38,42; Joel 1:4; 2:25; Amos 7:1-2). God directs armies as He directs all things!
These locusts gather the ill-gotten spoils of Assyria.

There are many Semitic words for this insect which apparently denote (see Joel 2:25)

- different species

- different stages of growth

verses.zh: 耶和华被尊崇，因他居在高处；他以公平公义充满锡安。
verses.en: The Lord is exalted,[NOTE:1] indeed,[NOTE:2] he lives in heaven;[NOTE:3] he fills Zion with justice and fairness.
notes: Or “elevated”; NCV, NLT “is very great.”
Or “for” (KJV, NASB, NIV).
Heb “on high” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); CEV “in the heavens.”
verses.commentary:
33:5 "He dwells on high" This phrase is imagery for the place of YHWH's abode (cf. Isa. 32:15; Job 16:19; 31:2).
The ANE viewed heaven as above. For the Israelites the smoke from their sacrifices rose to God, therefore,
He must be up. There was also the theological contrast with "down" as imagery for death. Sheol was down,
but heaven was up. In our modern era these spacial images seem inaccurate, but remember they are ancient
imagery never intended to carry literalness. The language of the OT is phenomenological, which means
the language of description using the five human senses. The Bible is not anti-scientific, it is
pre-scientific! Taking ancient imagery literally is not a sign of biblical conservatism, but of missing
the intended meaning of the original historical setting of the inspired authors.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "justice and righteousness" See note at Isa. 32:16 and
SPECIAL TOPIC: IMMANUEL'S PERSON AND REIGN.

verses.zh: 你一生一世必得安稳―有丰盛的救恩，并智慧和知识；你以敬畏耶和华为至宝。
verses.en: He is your constant source of stability;[NOTE:1] he abundantly provides safety and great wisdom;[NOTE:2] he gives all this to those who fear him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and he is the stability of your times.”
Heb “a rich store of deliverance, wisdom, and knowledge.”
Heb “the fear of the Lord, it is his treasure.”
verses.commentary:
33:6

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"He will be the stability of your times"

NJB
"You can count on this all your days"

Peshitta
"Faith shall be the stability of your times"

REB
"her strength will be in your unchanging

stability"

NET
"He is your constant source of stability"

YHWH brings "stability," lit. "faithful," BDB 53, cf. Isa. 25:1. Judah's hope and
stability is the faithful character of her God (cf. Deut. 32:4; Ps. 36:5; 89:1-2,5,24,33,49; 88:11;
92:2; 143:1). This is the answer to the prayer of Isa. 33:2. Because of His faithful character He gives
to His wayward people

- a wealth (BDB 340) of

- salvation (BDB 447)

- wisdom (BDB 315 with change of final consonant from ת to
ה, cf. Isa. 11:2)

- knowledge (BDB 395, cf. Isa. 11:2)

- the fear (BDB 432, in the sense of reverential awe, cf. Isa. 11:2; Prov. 1:7,29; 2:5) of YHWH is
his treasure (BDB 69, in the sense of a full storehouse, cf. 1 Chr. 27:27-28; 2 Chr. 11:11); see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

verses.zh: 看哪，他们的豪杰在外头哀号；求和的使臣痛痛哭泣。
verses.en: Look, ambassadors[NOTE:1] cry out in the streets;messengers sent to make peace[NOTE:2] weep bitterly.
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew word is unknown. Proposals include “heroes” (cf. KJV, ASV “valiant ones”; NASB, NIV “brave men”); “priests,” “residents [of Jerusalem].” The present translation assumes that the term is synonymous with “messengers of peace,” with which it corresponds in the parallel structure of the verse.
Heb “messengers of peace,” apparently those responsible for negotiating the agreements that have been broken (see v. 8).
verses.commentary:
33:7-9 This reflects the sad state of the impending siege because negotiations have failed
(cf. 2 Kgs. 18:13-16).

33:7 These two poetic lines may not be synonymous (LXX, Peshitta). Biblical scholars have been
influenced by Robert Lowth, who tried to fit all Hebrew parallelism into three or four categories. Today
scholars are understanding the multiplicity of poetic parallelism. Currently it is best to say that
the second line "adds something" or "goes beyond" (Adele Berlin, The Dynamics of Biblical Parallelism:
Revised and Expanded, p. 64).

There may be different groups addressed.

- line one ‒ soldiers of Jerusalem (JPSOA, "Arielites")

- line two ‒ the ambassador of peace sent to Egypt by Hezekiah (cf. Isa. 33:8; JPSOA)

- The Jewish Study Bible, p. 848, mentions that rabbinical texts see this verse as related to angels (messengers)
weeping over the fall of Zion

They do similar/parallel things

- "cry," BDB 858, KB 1042, Qal PERFECT

- "weep," BDB 113, KB 129, Qal IMPERFECT

Parallelism is one of the main keys in interpreting Hebrew poetry, but we must recognize it is
used in many forms and at many literary levels.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

NASB, TEV
"brave men"

NKJV, NRSV, REB
"valiant ones"

NJB
"Ariel"

JPSOA
"Arielites"

NET
"ambassadors"

The MT has אראלם
(BDB 72, KB 82), which is found only here. This root is

- similar to "Ariel" (KB 87 II, JPSOA, i.e. Jerusalem, cf. Isa. 29:1,2,7)

- similar to "warrior" (NASB, NKJV, Targums)

- "heroes" (KB 87 I)

- "priests" (KB 82)

- "ambassadors" (NET Bible, p. 1235, #13, which assumes a parallelism between the two lines of
poetry in v. 7

verses.zh: 大路荒凉，行人止息；敌人背约，藐视城邑，不顾人民。
verses.en: Highways are empty;[NOTE:1] there are no travelers.[NOTE:2] Treaties are broken;[NOTE:3] witnesses are despised;[NOTE:4] human life is treated with disrespect.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “desolate” (NAB, NASB); NIV, NRSV, NLT “deserted.”
Heb “the one passing by on the road ceases.”
Heb “one breaks a treaty”; NAB “Covenants are broken.”

The Hebrew text reads literally, “he despises cities.” The term עָרִים (ʿarim, “cities”) probably needs to be emended to an original עֵדִים (ʿedim, “[legal] witnesses”), a reading that is preserved in the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa. Confusion of dalet (ד) and resh (ר) is a well-attested scribal error.
Heb “he does not regard human beings.”
verses.commentary:
33:8

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"cities"

NRSV
"oaths"

NJB, RSV
"witnesses"

REB
"treaties"

TEV
"agreements"

DSS
"a pact"

The MT has "cities" (ערים,
BDB 746 and DSS), but because of the parallelism, "witnesses"
(עדים, BDB 729; DSS Isaiah scrolls) fits better.
This could be another "R" ‒ "D" confusion. The UBS Hebrew Text Project, p. 77 gives "witness"
a C rating (i.e. considerable doubt).

verses.zh: 地上悲哀衰残；黎巴嫩羞愧枯干；沙仑像旷野；巴珊和迦密的树林凋残。
verses.en: The land[NOTE:1] dries up[NOTE:2] and withers away;the forest of Lebanon shrivels up[NOTE:3] and decays.Sharon[NOTE:4] is like the arid rift valley;[NOTE:5] Bashan and Carmel[NOTE:6] are parched.[NOTE:7]
notes: Or “earth” (KJV); NAB “the country.”
Or “mourns” (BDB 5 s.v. I אָבַל). HALOT 6-7 lists homonyms I אבל (“mourn”) and II אבל (“dry up”). They propose the second here on the basis of parallelism. See 24:4.
Heb “Lebanon is ashamed.” The Hiphil is exhibitive, expressing the idea, “exhibits shame.” In this context the statement alludes to the withering of vegetation.
Sharon was a fertile plain along the Mediterranean coast. See 35:2.

The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) is a geographic feature extending from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba. Especially in the vicinity of the Dead Sea and then ranging southward, it is very dry with little vegetation.
Both of these areas were known for their trees and vegetation. See 2:13; 35:2.
Heb “shake off [their leaves]” (so ASV, NRSV); NAB “are stripped bare.”
verses.commentary:
33:9 This verse uses agricultural imagery for the problems involved in the Assyrian siege of
Jerusalem in 701 B.C. These types of agricultural imagery are common in
Isaiah (cf. Isa. 16:8; 24:4,7). YHWH controls the weather for His purposes (cf. Deuteronomy 27-28). There
is no distinction between the "natural" and "supernatural" in the Bible, as in the worldview of the ANE.
Deity is intimately involved in His creation. Be careful of your modern, scientific worldview placing a
theological grid over Scripture!

verses.zh: 耶和华说：现在我要起来；我要兴起；我要勃然而兴。
verses.en: “Now I will rise up,” says the Lord.“Now I will exalt myself;now I will magnify myself.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “lift myself up” (KJV); NLT “show my power and might.”
verses.commentary: 33:10-12 These possibly relate to Assyria as in Isa. 33:1.

verses.zh: 你们要怀的是糠秕，要生的是碎秸；你们的气就是吞灭自己的火。
verses.en: You conceive straw,[NOTE:1] you give birth to chaff;your breath is a fire that destroys you.[NOTE:2]
notes: The second person verb and pronominal forms in this verse are plural. The hostile nations are the addressed, as the next verse makes clear.
The hostile nations’ plans to destroy God’s people will come to nothing; their hostility will end up being self-destructive.
verses.commentary:
33:11-12 The imagery of "chaff" and "fire" are common in Isaiah
(cf. Isa. 1:7; 5:24; 9:18-19; 10:16-19; 26:11; 29:6; 30:27-28; 33:11-14; 47:14, also Joel 2:3). See
Special Topic: Fire.

Isaiah uses imagery from human reproduction.

- here, conception, BDB 247 I, KB 255, Qal imperfect, Isa. 8:3;
26:18; 59:4,13

- giving birth, Isa. 9:6; 13:8; 21:3; 23:4; 26:17,18; 39:7; 51:18; 54:1; 59:4; 66:7,9

▣ "My breath" This is the term ruah (BDB 924) used as an anthropomorphic imagery
for the wind of judgment from YHWH's nostrils (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT). It is obviously a way of showing YHWH's personal participation
(cf. Exodus 15:18; 2 Sam. 22:16; Ps. 18:15) in judgment (cf. Isa. 11:4; 30:28; 40:7).

verses.zh: 列邦必像已烧的石灰，像已割的荆棘在火中焚烧。
verses.en: The nations will be burned to ashes;[NOTE:1] like thornbushes that have been cut down, they will be set on fire.
notes: Heb “will be a burning to lime.” See Amos 2:1.

verses.zh: 你们远方的人当听我所行的；你们近处的人当承认我的大能。
verses.en: You who are far away, listen to what I have done!You who are close by, recognize my strength.”
verses.commentary:
33:13 "You who are far away. . .you who are near" In context, this refers to God's people in exile in
Assyria and to God's people still in Judah (cf. Dan. 9:7). However, seen in the wider context of the new age, it
may be related to the Gentile and the Jewish people (cf. Isa. 49:1; it is imagery for all, cf. Jer. 25:26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 锡安中的罪人都惧怕；不敬虔的人被战兢抓住。我们中间谁能与吞灭的火同住？我们中间谁能与永火同住呢？
verses.en: Sinners are afraid in Zion;panic[NOTE:1] grips the godless.[NOTE:2] They say,[NOTE:3] “Who among us can coexist with destructive fire?Who among us can coexist with unquenchable[NOTE:4] fire?”
notes: Or “trembling” (ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “shake with fear.”
Or “the defiled”; TEV “The sinful people of Zion”; NLT “The sinners in Jerusalem.”
The words “they say” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Or “perpetual”; or “everlasting” (KJV, ASV, NAB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
33:14 "Sinners in Zion are terrified" Again the reality of a mixture of the faithful and unfaithful
within the people of God is acknowledged. Sinners

- are terrified, BDB 808, KB 922, Qal PERFECT, cf. NOUN ‒ Isa. 2:10,19,21; 24:17,18;
VERB ‒ 12:2; 19:16,17; 44:8,11; 51:13

- trembling has seized the godless, BDB 28, KB 31, Qal PERFECT, cf. Isa. 13:8; 21:3

The "godless" (BDB 338) are described in Isa. 32:6 as those who practice godlessness and speak
error against the Lord (cf. Isa. 9:17; 10:6).

▣ "Who among us can live with the consuming fire?

Who among us can live with the continual burning" This refers to God's holiness as seen
through the imagery of fire connected with His righteousness and His judgment (cf. Deut. 4:24; 5:24;
Isa. 30:27,30).

For "continual" (lit. "forever") see Special Topic: Forever ('olam).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

verses.zh: 行事公义、说话正直、憎恶欺压的财利、摆手不受贿赂、塞耳不听流血的话，闭眼不看邪恶事的，
verses.en: The one who lives[NOTE:1] uprightly[NOTE:2] and speaks honestly,the one who refuses to profit from oppressive measuresand rejects a bribe,[NOTE:3] the one who does not plot violent crimes[NOTE:4] and does not seek to harm others[NOTE:5]—
notes: Heb “walks” (so NASB, NIV).
Or, possibly, “justly”; NAB “who practices virtue.”
Heb “[who] shakes off his hands from grabbing hold of a bribe.”
Heb “[who] shuts his ear from listening to bloodshed.”
Heb “[who] closes his eyes from seeing evil.”
verses.commentary:
33:15 This reflects the character of YHWH as seen in His people.

- walks righteously

- speaks with sincerity

- rejects unjust gain

- does not take a bribe

- does not listen to evil plans (i.e. bloodshed)

- does not look upon evil

verses.zh: 他必居高处；他的保障是磐石的坚垒；他的粮必不缺乏（原文是赐给）；他的水必不断绝。
verses.en: this is the person who will live in a secure place;[NOTE:1] he will find safety in the rocky, mountain strongholds;[NOTE:2] he will have foodand a constant supply of water.
notes: Heb “he [in the] exalted places will live.”
Heb “mountain strongholds, cliffs [will be] his elevated place.”
verses.commentary:
33:16 The person who lives the life described in Isa. 33:15

- will dwell on the heights

- will take refuge in the impregnable rock

- will have an abundance of food

- will have a sure water supply

This describes the new age person. The ideal of Deuteronomy is actualized!

verses.zh: 你的眼必见王的荣美，必见辽阔之地。
verses.en: You will see a king in his splendor;[NOTE:1] you will see a wide land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your eyes will see a king in his beauty”; NIV, NRSV “the king.”
Heb “a land of distances,” i.e., an extensive land.
verses.commentary:
33:17 "Your eyes will see" This VERB (BDB 302, KB 301) is often used to
refer to spiritual insight (cf. Isa. 26:11; 33:17,20; 48:6; Job 23:8-9; Ps. 46:8; 63:2). Humans were
created to function in two realms.

- the physical (i.e. nephesh, this planet)

- the spiritual (i.e. ruah, fellowship with God)

The Fall of Genesis 3 has disrupted both!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ "the King and his beauty" This is a purposeful ambiguity, much like Isa. 32:1, where the
context fits both Hezekiah in his day and the coming Messiah of Isa. 7:14.

verses.zh: 你的心必思想那惊吓的事，自问说：记数目的在哪里呢？平贡银的在哪里呢？数戍楼的在哪里呢？
verses.en: Your mind will recall the terror you experienced,[NOTE:1] and you will ask yourselves,[NOTE:2] “Where is the scribe?Where is the one who weighs the money?Where is the one who counts the towers?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “your heart will meditate on terror.”
The words “and you will ask yourselves” are supplied in the translation for clarification and stylistic reasons.
The people refer to various Assyrian officials who were responsible for determining the amount of taxation or tribute Judah must pay to the Assyrian king.
verses.commentary: 33:18 "Where is he who counts" This refers to Assyrian scouts reconnoitering Jerusalem for the coming siege.

verses.zh: 你必不见那强暴的民，就是说话深奥，你不能明白，言语呢喃，你不能懂得的。
verses.en: You will no longer see a defiant[NOTE:1] peoplewhose language you do not comprehend,[NOTE:2] whose derisive speech you do not understand.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew form נוֹעָז (noʿaz) is a Niphal participle derived from יָעַז (yaʿaz, an otherwise unattested verb) or from עָזָז (ʿazaz, “be strong,” unattested elsewhere in the Niphal). Some prefer to emend the form to לוֹעֵז (loʿez) which occurs in Ps 114:1 with the meaning “speak a foreign language.” See HALOT 809 s.v. עזז, 533 s.v. לעז. In this case, one might translate “people who speak a foreign language.”
Heb “a people too deep of lip to hear.” The phrase “deep of lip” must be an idiom meaning “lips that speak words that are unfathomable [i.e., incomprehensible].”
Heb “derision of tongue there is no understanding.” The Niphal of לָעַג (laʿag) occurs only here. In the Qal and Hiphil the verb means “to deride, mock.” A related noun is used in 28:11.
verses.commentary:
33:19

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"a fierce people"

NRSV, NJB
"the insolent people"

TEV
"arrogant foreigners"

REB, JPSOA
"barbarous people"

NET
"a defiant people"

The PARTICIPLE describing "people" is BDB 418, KB 420, Niphal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, and is found only here. Some scholars take it from another
root, "to be strong" (BDB 738), but it has never been found in the Niphal stem.

There is one more interpretive option. Take it from another root (BDB 541, KB 533, Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE), "to stammer" or "speak unintelligibly," which is used in the third line
of v. 19, thereby paralleling all three lines.

NASB, NJB
"unintelligible speech"

NKJV, NRSV, REB, JPSOA
"obscure speech"

LXX
"deep speech"

Peshitta
"deeper speech"

The MT has the ADJECTIVE (BDB 771, KB 849) "deep" or "unfathomable"
(cf. Ezek. 3:5-6). This relates to YHWH's warning of His sending foreign invaders into Canaan if His people do not
keep His law (cf. Deut. 28:49). They did not; He did (cf. Isa. 28:11; Jer. 5:15). In this context,
it refers to Assyria.

Paul uses this imagery to describe speaking in tongues in the NT (cf. 1 Cor. 14:21).

verses.zh: 你要看锡安―我们守圣节的城！你的眼必见耶路撒冷为安静的居所，为不挪移的帐幕，橛子永不拔出，绳索一根也不折断。
verses.en: Look at Zion, the city where we hold religious festivals!You[NOTE:1] will see Jerusalem,[NOTE:2] a peaceful settlement,a tent that stays put;[NOTE:3] its stakes will never be pulled up;none of its ropes will snap in two.
notes: Heb “your eyes” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Or “that does not travel”; NASB “which shall not be folded.”
verses.commentary:
33:20 This is Isaiah's recurrent theology (with a few exceptions) that Jerusalem will never fall (cf. Isaiah 36-37). For a full
discussion of "city" see notes at Isa. 24:10 and the chart at the Introduction to chapter 26, D. This
prophecy must be understood in context because in Jeremiah's day, God gave exactly the opposite prophecy.

The imagery of "a tent" is an anachronistic allusion back to the Exodus (cf. Job 4:21; Isa. 38:12; 54:2; Jer. 10:20).
It may also denote "the tabernacle" built as a portable tent. The same allusion (i.e. tent) is used in Isa. 54:2 for a
worldwide expansion.

verses.zh: 在那里，耶和华必显威严与我们同在，当作江河宽阔之地；其中必没有荡桨摇橹的船来往，也没有威武的船经过。
verses.en: Instead the Lord will rule there as our mighty king.[NOTE:1] Rivers and wide streams will flow through it;[NOTE:2] no war galley will enter;[NOTE:3] no large ships will sail through.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “But there [as] a mighty one [will be] the Lord for us.”
Heb “a place of rivers, streams wide of hands [i.e., on both sides].”
Heb “a ship of rowing will not go into it.”
Heb “and a mighty ship will not pass through it.”
verses.commentary:
33:21 The imagery of "rivers and sailing ships" seems to be a play on their alliances with Egypt
(cf. Isa. 33:23). Instead of Egypt, YHWH (the Majestic One) will be their provider and protector
(cf. Isa. 33:22).

verses.zh: 因为，耶和华是审判我们的；耶和华是给我们设律法的；耶和华是我们的王；他必拯救我们。
verses.en: For the Lord, our ruler,the Lord, our commander,the Lord, our king—he will deliver us.
verses.commentary:
33:22 Jerusalem (cf. Isa. 33:20) is again the city of the Great King (YHWH Himself) as represented
in His righteous surrogate (the Davidic Messiah).

YHWH is

- Judge (BDB 1047)

- Lawgiver (BDB 349)

- King (BDB 572 I)

- Savior (BDB 446; see SPECIAL TOPIC: OUR SAVIOR)

verses.zh: 你的绳索松开：不能栽稳桅杆，也不能扬起篷来。那时许多掳来的物被分了；瘸腿的把掠物夺去了。
verses.en: Though at this time your ropes are slack,[NOTE:1] the mast is not secured,[NOTE:2] and the sail[NOTE:3] is not unfurled,at that time you will divide up a great quantity of loot;[NOTE:4] even the lame will drag off plunder.[NOTE:5]
notes: The words “though at this time” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The first half of the verse is addressed to Judah and contrasts the nation’s present weakness with its future prosperity. Judah is compared to a ship that is incapable of sailing.
Heb “they do not fasten the base of their mast.” On כֵּן (ken, “base”) see BDB 487 s.v. III כֵּן and HALOT 483 s.v. III כֵּן.
Or perhaps, “flag.”
Heb “then there will be divided up loot of plunder [in] abundance.”
Judah’s victory over its enemies will be so thorough there will be more than enough plunder for everyone, even slow-moving lame men who would normally get left out in the rush to gather the loot.
verses.commentary:
33:23 Poetry is ambiguous. This could refer to

- the destruction of Assyria

- the empowering of Jerusalem

- or both

In Isaiah 33:17, both "your eyes" and "they will behold" have uncertain antecedents. Isaiah 33:18
seems to refer to Assyria checking out Jerusalem for invasion and siege. Isaiah 33:19 seems to allude
to the strange-sounding language of the Assyrian invaders. Yet at Isa. 33:20 the scene changes to an
undisturbed Jerusalem. Therefore, Isa. 33:21 and 22 could refer to Jerusalem, obviously Isa. 33:24 does.

Some see the "plunder" (BDB 1021) in Isa. 33:23 as related to the items that the Assyrian
army abandoned before the walls of Jerusalem in 701 B.C. (NEB) and not the sack
of Nineveh itself, which occurred in 612 B.C. by the Neo-Babylonian and Median armies.

verses.zh: 城内居民必不说：我病了；其中居住的百姓，罪孽都赦免了。
verses.en: No resident of Zion[NOTE:1] will say, “I am ill”;the people who live there will have their sin forgiven.
notes: The words “of Zion” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
33:24 YHWH is characterized as the healer. This is an allusion to chapter 1 where God's faithless people
are characterized as ill (cf. Isa. 1:5-6). Illness is imagery for "sin" and "rebellion"
(cf. Ps. 41:4; 103:3; Isa. 53:5). The NT continues the Jewish concept of sickness relating to sin
(cf. John 5:14; James 5:14-15). See SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

This is such a powerful verse! Not only is physical healing an aspect of God's people's
restoration, but also complete forgiveness (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS [OT]). This VERB
"will be forgiven," has the basic connotation of "to lift up and bear away" (i.e. Exod. 32:32; 34:7;
Num. 14:18-19; Ps. 32:1,5; 85:2).

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The paragraphing is ambiguous (because of the composite nature of these poems) in this
chapter. Several different groups are addressed.

- Assyria, Isa. 33:1

- covenant people, Isa. 33:2

- brave men who cry in the streets, Isa. 33:7

- ambassadors of peace who weep, Isa. 33:7

- the traveler, Isa. 33:8

- the people, Isa. 33:12

- you who are far away, Isa. 33:13

- you who are near, Isa. 33:13

- sinners in Zion, Isa. 33:14

- he who walks righteously, Isa. 33:15

- He. . .His, Isa. 33:16

- your heart, Isa. 33:18-20

- your tackle, Isa. 33:23

- resident. . .people, Isa. 33:24

It is difficult to identify the groups to which each of these relate.

- Notice how many names/titles and characterizations of Israel's God are mentioned in this chapter.

- YHWH, Isa. 33:2

- YHWH is exalted, Isa. 33:5,10

- He shall be the stability (lit. "faithfulness"), Isa. 33:6

- a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge, Isa. 33:6

- the fear of YHWH, Isa. 33:6

- King in His beauty, Isa. 33:17

- the majestic One, Isa. 33:21

- several, "The Lord is. . .," Isa. 33:22

- It is possible that the first section of Isaiah ends after this chapter because the DSS
scroll of Isaiah has a double space after this chapter, but no break after chapter 39.

- "Possible" outline of the poem's order/arrangement

- God judges Assyria who He used to judge Judah, Isa. 33:1

- Judah prays for help, Isa. 33:2

- God responds, Isa. 33:3-6,10-12

- Judah's current state, Isa. 33:7-9

- the godly spared, Isa. 33:13-16

- a recapitulation of the Assyrian period, Isa. 33:17-20

- the reign of the righteous king, Isa. 33:21-24

1Woe to you, O destroyer,

8The highways are desolate, the traveler has ceased,

9The land mourns and pines away,
